entries.title: WiseTech says Australian police took no action against founder Richard White after probing allegations he exploited a woman's immigration status for sex (Angus Whitley/Bloomberg)
Trump says a pardon for Jensen Huang is "always an option" but likely unnecessary, and it's "probably not too late" for the US to take an equity stake in Nvidia (New York Post)
Jensen Huang's return is greeted with relief in China, with state media saying "The king is back!", as Asian stocks jump; Taiwan hailed him as a hometown hero (Washington Post)
Anthropic rolls out "Install as app" in beta, which turns Claude artifacts into Mac and Windows apps with notifications, optional full computer access, and more (Claude)
Dell reports Q3 revenue up 103% YoY to $54.94B, above $49.32B est., and raises its annual revenue and profit forecasts for the third time this year (Reuters)
Anthropic details Siren, a honeypot test that tempts AI agents to escape sandboxes; its newer models fell for it 0.6%-1.6% of the time, vs. 25.8% for Mythos 5 (Will Knight/Wired)
Docs: Grubhub is on track for ~$6.4B in GTV and a $97M EBITDA loss in 2026, reflecting heavy marketing and operating costs; Wonder says it's not pursuing a sale (Valida Pau/The Information)
A judge orders the ex-OpenAI staffer charged with bugging an exec conference room released on $1M bond, finding prosecutors lack evidence to keep him in custody (Bloomberg)
A US jury finds Huawei guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets and bank fraud but acquits it of the most severe charge of criminal racketeering conspiracy (Associated Press)
Sources: Jensen Huang said Nvidia doesn't need a succession plan because it operates a unique business model and such a plan would create unnecessary hierarchy (CNBC)
Sources: the CIA, ODNI, and NGA found a breach of an open-source intelligence system that exposed some unclassified info; hackers likely used the AI tool Artex (New York Times)
President Trump finds himself isolated in DC over his moves to reinstate Jensen Huang as even some of his staunchest allies vow to probe Huang and Nvidia (CNBC)
Jensen Huang says he is back not as a "tech bro" or due to Trump's pressure, but because Nvidia's board "evaluated the entire situation" and "gathered facts" (New York Times)
AG Todd Blanche and FBI Director Kash Patel dodge reporters' questions about a purported probe that led Trump to push Nvidia's board to bring back Jensen Huang (Dan Mangan/CNBC)
Tidal will ban fully AI-generated music starting December 9 and says such content accounted for ~43% of tracks distributed to its platform over the past 90 days (Ethan Millman/The Hollywood Reporter)
